purpose: Landmark gameplay definitions transcribed from the physical tiles and player aid.
photoOrientation: Positions below assume the photo is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise, so the cards are upright.

sharedRules.timing: Landmark effects are immediate and used once when gained.

additionalCostSymbol.description: Every tile begins its cost row with a yellow circle containing a black tower/fortress silhouette.
additionalCostSymbol.meaning: Pay one coin per friendly fortress already on the central board, before placement.

landmarks.name: Barad-dûr

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Take all discarded cards, secretly choose 1, and play it for free.

landmarks.name: Bree

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Place 1 fortress and 2 units in Arnor.
Complete 2 movements on the central board.

landmarks.name: Erebor

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Complete 1 movement on the central board.

landmarks.name: Grey Havens

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Take the top 2 tokens of any one race and reveal them. Choose 1 to place in front of you. Return the second token face down to the top of its stack.

landmarks.name: Helm’s Deep

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Place 1 fortress and 3 units in Rohan.

landmarks.name: Isengard

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Discard 1 grey card from the opponent’s play area.
Move your character 1 space on the Quest of the Ring track.

landmarks.name: Minas Tirith

cost.status: Resource counts transcribed from photo; fortress surcharge verified in rulebook.

effects: Place 1 fortress and 1 unit in Gondor.
Move your character 2 spaces on the Quest of the Ring track.

notes: Landmark names and destination regions come from the player aid; the photographed tiles have no printed names.
